newsitem.title: USA: High court rejects appeal on Calif. gang measure.
newsitem.headline: High court rejects appeal on Calif. gang measure.

text.p: The Supreme Court Friday rejected a challenge to a broad injunction in California that barred gang members from gathering in public or annoying people in a neighbourhood dominated by gang violence.

The justices let stand a California Supreme Court ruling that cities may use public nuisance laws to obtain injunctions to prevent suspected gang members from taking part in what otherwise would be legal activitiy.

The city of San Jose obtained the injunction in 1993 to prevent 38 Hispanic men and women alleged to be members of a criminal street gang from frequenting a four-block neighbourhood described as "an urban war zone."

The city charged that the gang members, who live elsewhere, had taken over the neighbourhood, openly engaging in criminal activity, including murder, assault, arson and illegal drug use. Residents were afraid to come out of their homes.
One provision of the injunction barred a gang member from "standing, sitting, walking, driving, gathering or appearing in public view" with other gang members.

The other challenged provision barred gang members from "confronting, intimidating, annonying, harassing, threatening, challenging, provoking or assaulting" residents, especially those who have complained to the police. Violators of the injunction faced up to six months in jail and a $1,000 fine.
Lawyers from civil rights groups, representing two suspected gang members, appealed to the Supreme Court, asking the justices to hear the case and strike down the injunction as unconstitutional.
The Supreme Court sided with city authorities, rejecting the appeal without any comment or dissent.
